title: Employee ID Generator
statement: Create an Employee class that generates a unique employee ID for every employee. The first employee must receive ID 1001, the next 1002, and so on. Use a static variable to maintain the ID and another static variable to count the total number of employees.
constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000
1 <= name.length() <= 50
Name contains only alphabets.
Initial ID is 1001.
explanation: nextId is static, so it is shared among all employee objects. For every object: (1) Assign nextId to id, (2) Increment nextId, (3) Increment employee count.

title: Bank Account Generator
sampleOutput:
ACC5001 Alice
ACC5002 Bob
ACC5003 John
ACC5004 David
statement: Generate unique bank account numbers starting from 5001.
explanation: nextAccount belongs to the class rather than an individual object. Therefore, every object receives a different account number.

title: Static Block Configuration
statement: Use a static block to initialize: Company name = ByteXL, Base employees = 100. The input represents newly joined employees.
explanation: The static block executes automatically when the Company class is loaded.

title: Product Discount Calculator
statement: All products receive the same discount percentage. Store the discount in a static variable and calculate the final price using a static method.
explanation: Discount amount = price × discount / 100. Final price = price - discount amount.

title: Object Counter
statement: Count the total number of objects created using a static variable.
explanation: Every constructor execution increments the same static count.

title: Static and Instance Initialization Order
concept: Static block vs instance block vs constructor
sampleOutput:
Static Block
Main Started
Instance Block
Constructor
Instance Block
Constructor
Main Ended
statement: Demonstrate the execution order of: (1) Static block, (2) Main method, (3) Instance block, (4) Constructor.
explanation: The static block executes only once when the class is loaded. The instance block and constructor execute every time an object is created.

title: Static Tax Calculator
statement: Create a static tax rate applicable to all employees. Calculate tax for every salary.
explanation: Tax is calculated as salary × taxRate / 100.

title: Static Prime Utility
sampleOutput:
Prime
Not Prime
Prime
Not Prime
Prime
statement: Create a utility class containing a static method isPrime().
explanation: A number is prime if it has no divisor between 2 and sqrt(n).

title: Static Configuration Manager
statement: Use a static block to initialize default application configuration: Environment = Development, MaxUsers = 100. Then update the configuration using a static method.
explanation: The static block provides default configuration. The static update() method modifies the shared class-level values.

title: Static Employee Salary Statistics
statement: Create an Employee class where: every employee stores an individual salary, a static variable stores total salary, a static variable stores employee count, and a static method returns average salary.
explanation: Every object updates the shared count and totalSalary. average = totalSalary / count.

title: Employee Salary Using Runtime Polymorphism
statement: Create a base Employee class. Developer gets 10% bonus. Manager gets 20% bonus. Override calculateSalary().
constraints:
Salary: 0-10^9
Type is either Developer or Manager.
explanation: The reference variable is of type Employee, but the actual object is Developer. Therefore Java invokes the overridden calculateSalary() method at runtime.

title: Shape Area Using Abstraction
statement: Create an abstract class Shape. Implement Circle, Rectangle, and Triangle. Each class must implement area().
constraints:
Dimensions are positive.
0 < radius, length, width, base, height <= 10^6
explanation: Shape defines what every shape must provide, but does not specify how the area is calculated. Each subclass provides its own implementation.

title: Payment System Using Interface
statement: Create a Payment interface and implement UPI, CreditCard, and NetBanking.
explanation: The interface defines a common pay() contract. Each implementation decides how the payment is performed.

title: Vehicle Hierarchy
statement: Create a base class Vehicle and subclasses: Car (18 km/l), Bike (45 km/l), Truck (8 km/l). Override calculateMileage().
constraints: Type is one of the three specified types.
explanation: The same reference type Vehicle can point to different subclass objects.

title: Notification System
statement: Create a Notification interface with implementations: Email, SMS, Push.
explanation: The interface provides abstraction and allows different notification classes to follow the same contract.
timeComplexity: O(L) where L is message length

title: Abstract Employee Bonus
statement: Create an abstract Employee class. Developer bonus = 15%. Manager bonus = 25%.
explanation: Because calculateBonus() is abstract, each subclass must implement its own bonus logic.

title: Multiple Interfaces
statement: Create two interfaces: Printable, Scannable. Create a Printer class that implements both.
explanation: Java does not support multiple inheritance through classes, but a class can implement multiple interfaces.

title: Banking Polymorphism
statement: Create: Account, SavingsAccount, CurrentAccount. Savings account interest = 6%. Current account interest = 2%.
explanation: The method invoked depends on the actual object created, demonstrating runtime polymorphism.

title: Abstract Notification Validation
statement: Create an abstract Notification class with validate() and send(). Email is valid if it contains '@'. SMS is valid if its length is exactly 10.
constraints:
Message length: 1-100
SMS contains digits.
Email contains at least one '@'.
explanation: The base class defines the general notification behavior. Each subclass provides its own validation rule.

title: E-Commerce Product Hierarchy
statement: Create an abstract Product class. Electronics -> 18% tax. Clothing -> 10% discount. Grocery -> 5% tax. Calculate the final price.
explanation: Each subclass applies its own pricing rule through method overriding.

title: First Non-Repeating Character
statement: Find the first character that occurs exactly once.
constraints:
1 <= length <= 100000
String contains lowercase English letters.
explanation: Frequencies: s -> 3, w -> 1, i -> 1. The first character having frequency 1 is w.

title: Remove Duplicate Characters
statement: Remove duplicate characters while preserving their first occurrence.
explanation: Characters are added to the result only the first time they are encountered.

title: Longest Word in a Sentence
statement: Find the longest word in a sentence. If two words have the same length, return the first one.
constraints:
1 <= sentence.length() <= 100000
Words are separated by spaces.
explanation: The word lengths are: Java -> 4, programming -> 11, language -> 7. Therefore programming is longest.

title: String Compression
statement: Compress consecutive characters. Example: aaabbccccd becomes a3b2c4d1.
constraints:
1 <= length <= 100000
String contains lowercase English letters.
explanation: Count consecutive occurrences of each character and append both the character and its count using StringBuilder.

title: Anagram Without Sorting
statement: Determine whether two strings are anagrams without sorting them.
constraints:
1 <= length <= 100000
Strings contain lowercase English letters.
explanation: Both strings contain exactly the same frequency of every character.

title: Palindrome Ignoring Spaces and Case
sampleInput: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
statement: Determine whether a sentence is a palindrome after ignoring spaces, case, and special characters.
explanation: After removing non-alphanumeric characters and converting to lowercase: amanaplanacanalpanama. It reads the same forward and backward.

title: Reverse Words
statement: Reverse the order of words without reversing individual characters.
explanation: The words are stored and processed from the last word to the first.

title: String Rotation
statement: Determine whether string B is a rotation of string A.
constraints:
1 <= length <= 100000
Both strings contain lowercase letters.
explanation: If B is a rotation of A, then B must be present inside A + A. For example, ABCDABCD contains CDAB.
timeComplexity: O(N) average for the practical string-search approach

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
statement: Find the length of the longest substring containing no repeated characters.
explanation: The longest substrings without repetition include abc, which has length 3. A sliding-window approach maintains the current unique substring.

title: Compare Strings Without equals()
statement: Implement your own string comparison method without using equals() or compareTo(). Return true only when both strings are exactly identical.
explanation: First compare lengths. If they are equal, compare every corresponding character.

title: Matrix Multiplication
statement: Multiply two matrices. Matrix multiplication is possible only if columns of A = rows of B.
explanation: Each result cell is calculated as result[i][j] = sum of a[i][k] x b[k][j].

title: Spiral Matrix Traversal
statement: Print the elements of a matrix in spiral order.
explanation: Maintain four boundaries: top, bottom, left, right. Process one outer layer at a time.

title: Rotate Matrix 90 Degrees
statement: Rotate a square matrix by 90 degrees clockwise in-place.
explanation: A clockwise rotation can be achieved using two operations: (1) Transpose the matrix, (2) Reverse every row.

title: Row With Maximum Sum
statement: Find the row having the maximum sum. Return the row number using 1-based indexing.
explanation: Row sums: Row 1 -> 6, Row 2 -> 11, Row 3 -> 6. Therefore row 2 is selected.

title: Saddle Point in Matrix
statement: Find an element that is minimum in its row and maximum in its column. Such an element is called a saddle point.
explanation: Note: the naive 1-9 ascending matrix example is a common ambiguity trap for this definition -- its row-minimums are not column-maximums, so it yields no saddle point. The corrected sample below is consistent with the stated definition. Here 3 is the minimum in its row (3, 4, 5) and, checking its column (3, 2, 1), it is also the maximum in that column.

title: Diagonal Difference
statement: Calculate the absolute difference between the primary and secondary diagonal sums of a square matrix.
explanation: Primary diagonal: 1 + 5 + 9 = 15. Secondary diagonal: 3 + 5 + 7 = 15. Difference: |15 - 15| = 0.

title: Encapsulated Bank Account
statement: Create a BankAccount class where balance is private. Implement deposit(), withdraw(), getBalance(). Withdrawal should fail when the amount is greater than the available balance.
explanation: balance cannot be directly modified outside the class because it is private. The class controls access through public methods.

title: Utility Class for Array Operations
statement: Create a utility class similar to one that could be placed inside a package such as utilities. Implement static methods: maximum(), minimum(), average().
explanation: A utility class contains reusable static methods, so an object does not need to be created.

title: Encapsulated Student Result
statement: Create a Student class where marks are private. Implement setMarks(), getMarks(), calculateAverage(), calculateGrade(). Grade rules: >=90 A, >=75 B, >=60 C, >=50 D, otherwise F.
explanation: The marks array is private, so outside code cannot directly modify it. The public methods provide controlled access. Average = (80+90+70)/3 = 80, so grade is B.

title: Matrix Analyzer Using Encapsulation
sampleOutput:
Maximum: 9
Minimum: 1
Maximum Row: 3
Maximum Column: 3
Diagonal Sum: 12
statement: Create a MatrixAnalyzer class where the matrix is private. Implement public methods to find: maximum element, minimum element, row with maximum sum, column with maximum sum, main diagonal sum.
constraints:
1 <= R,C <= 500
Matrix values: -10^6 to 10^6
Matrix can be rectangular.
Diagonal sum is calculated for min(R,C) elements.
explanation: Row sums: Row1=9, Row2=16, Row3=20, so max row = 3. Column sums: Col1=13, Col2=14, Col3=18, so max column = 3. Main diagonal: 1 + 2 + 9 = 12.
